static_findings.finding: The independently reproduced old tiny_http idle-reader admission race belongs to transport connection ownership. Hyper HTTP/1 and Tokio independently scheduled connection tasks remove that shared reader pool without browser retries or longer acceptance deadlines.

Selected-root validation, canonical path fence, method policy, MIME mapping and no-cache policy remain concrete and unchanged in meaning. URL announcement follows selection validation and successful bind.

Listener admits each socket into its own task. That task owns the socket/service. ReaderStream body owns its Tokio file; poll-driven body/socket I/O yields under backpressure. Malformed/disconnected socket failure ends that connection; listener/runtime errors return process failure.
Explicit Content-Length frames full and streamed responses. Hyper suppresses HEAD body; independent pipelined GET/HEAD/GET exact-byte framing passed. No whole-file asset collection is introduced.

Only required HTTP/1 server and Tokio runtime/net/fs/io features are selected. tiny_http is removed. Local pinned Hyper/Tokio/ReaderStream source ownership agrees with production use; no router/framework or bespoke codec added.

limits: Own fixed execution is Linux portable HTTP only; browser, native suite, wheel, package and hosted-platform runs belong to coordinator or CI.

Held-open phase observations are finite (0.5 seconds); old source ownership explains structural starvation. Fixed probes establish progress for specified workloads, not universal liveness/resource limits.

Retained synchronous canonicalization/stat has no universal filesystem latency guarantee; canonical path check versus subsequent open preserves existing local-preview mutable-filesystem scope rather than asserting atomic adversarial containment.
Malformed/disconnect isolation is statically reviewed, not a new independently executed malformed-client test.
Hosted platform CI remains a gate; this is bounded foundation review, not release authorization.
